articles.title: ‘That was what you live for’: Fleetwood revel in ‘unbelievably special’ Arsenal win
articles.summary: Manager Matt Lawlor, born and raised in area, reflects on celebrating win with ‘people that I knew and grew up with’ Fleetwood’s manager, Matt Lawlor, hailed the club’s victory as one for all football after his side shocked the Premier League champions, Arsenal, on penalties in the Carabao Cup.
body: The goalkeeper, Jay Lynch, was Fleetwood’s other hero, saving from Bruno Guimarães to set up the chance for victory. Aaron Loupalo‑Bi and Viktor Gyökeres ensured it finished 1-1 in normal time, but Arsenal ended up a man light after Max Dowman was shown a red card for reacting to a challenge.

Asked if Fleetwood’s win was the story of the season, Lawlor said: “Yeah, I hope so. Football’s getting a little bit more, I don’t know, clinical and sanitised. And that to me there was that feeling that we all get as football fans. That was what you kind of live for, isn’t it? To be a part of it is special. To be giving that to football fans, and especially Fleetwood fans, is unbelievably special. And yeah, something that I’m really proud of.”

articles.title: Barcelona fined £503 over their approach for Atlético Madrid star Álvarez
articles.summary: Atlético accused Barcelona during summer chase. Striker now rebuilding his reputation with fans. Barcelona’s pursuit of Julián Álvarez came at a modest cost ⁠on Tuesday after the Spanish FA fined the club €602 (£503) following a complaint by Atlético Madrid over contact ⁠with ​the striker.
body: Atlético accused Barcelona of approaching the Argentine, whose contract runs until June 2030, ⁠without first notifying them in writing.
The sanction falls under Article 133 of the federation’s regulations. Atlético ⁠also complained to Fifa, which declared it had no ​jurisdiction over the case.

The striker scored Atlético’s ‌winner against Deportivo La Coruna on Saturday, finding the net for a second successive match as his side moved within two points of the La Liga leaders Barcelona, before apologising for expressing his desire to join their rivals.

“It ‌was a mistake. I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, ​I’d be angry too. Especially given how they’ve supported me since I arrived,” Álvarez said referring to an interview during the 2026 World Cup in which he said that ⁠he “wanted to fulfil his dream” of playing for ​Barcelona, triggering ​a transfer dispute that ​stretched through the summer transfer window.

articles.title: 'Biggest night in the club's history' for fearless Fleetwood
articles.summary: A whopping 83 league places separated Fleetwood from Arsenal, yet the hosts booked their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-final thanks to their penalty shootout win over the Gunners.
body: Given their league positions, form and pedigree there could only have been one winner predicted.

For the Cod Army, who won six promotions in 12 years in their impressive journey from non-league, this result will surely be remembered longest of all. Against the reigning Premier League champions, the club from a small seaside town in Lancashire created history in claiming one of the biggest cup upsets ever.
Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts the lead after 21 minutes but, after the break, Viktor Gyokeres pulled the visitors level.

And from there, they might have been expected to take charge but Fleetwood remained resolute, prospering from a wasteful performance from Arsenal that included Max Dowman being sent off for kicking out after a robust challenge from Harrison Neal.

articles.title: Fantastic Fleetwood seal shootout success in Carabao Cup shock against Arsenal
articles.summary: It is more than 20 years since Arsenal played at Highbury but their trip to League Two Fleetwood – and a stadium of the same name – did not bring back fond memories as they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup on penalties.
body: Aaron Loupalo-Bi and Viktor Gyökeres exchanged goals in normal time but Arsenal were unable to find a winner, despite being the dominant force, as Fleetwood battled to the end. The home manager, Matt Lawlor, was almost in tears, unable to cope after the tension was released when Conor Haughey smashed the ball into the top corner to settle the shootout.

That came after Jay Lynch had saved from Bruno Guimarães, a former warehouse worker stopping the Brazilian international. It is the storylines everyone wants but so rarely gets in the sanitised modern football world.

Fleetwood were aiming to earn £400,000 from the night but got something priceless in the end. Everyone in attendance will never forget they saw the fourth-tier side knock out the Premier League champions. Of course they had to ride their luck and were helped by Max Dowman’s debatable sending off but football is rarely about logic, it is one of emotion. This is once in a lifetime for the Cod Army, for anyone at their level, and they enjoyed it.

articles.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
articles.summary: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows. Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape.
body: Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure. Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door.

Beyond Busby and Ferguson, each United manager who also served felt the lash of desperation of a falling giant. Each of their defenestrations has featured an infighting that would not have been out of place in ancient Rome. Favouritism, nepotism, self-interest, entitlement, complacency and sentimentality have been the betrayal of a legend, to use the title of Michael Crick’s and David Smith’s “ j’accuse ” book from 1989. Living with the legend and influence of those two managers leads the list of difficulties.

Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United.

articles.title: Dowman sees red as Arsenal dumped out, but did Arteta go too far?
articles.summary: A shocking defeat, a red card card, a penalty-shootout and a drone tell the story of Arsenal's dramatic loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup.
body: Max Dowman is used to grabbing headlines for producing moments of magic but, after being sent off in just his second start of the season as Arsenal suffered a shock loss to Fleetwood Town, the 16-year-old is facing the first test of his short career.
Dowman scored twice as Arsenal beat Ipswich in the previous round of the Carabao Cup and manager Mikel Arteta rewarded him with another start in the last-16 tie at Fleetwood.
And this one was perhaps more of a chance than it looked. Arsenal are currently light on options in the wing with Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke all injured.

But, after being held by Fleetwood during normal time where the Gunners went behind despite having 26 shots and 78% possession, the Premier League champions lost on penalties following Dowman's red card, after a 1-1 draw in normal time.

articles.title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
articles.summary: Arsenal's match with Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup is delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone is spotted above the stadium during the match.
body: Arsenal's match against Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone was flown above the stadium while play was ongoing.
Referee Michael Salisbury stopped proceedings with one minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch while Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium.
The game was halted while the referee spoke to the management and staff on both benches, with police also investigating. A commentator for Sky later said police had located the drone operator.
The match got back under way with 10 minutes on the clock, with Fleetwood going on to complete a famous upset on penalties.

articles.title: Arteta explains reaction to Dowman red card amid criticism
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta has explained his reaction to Max Dowman as the 16-year-old went down the tunnel after being sent off in Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.
body: Moments before Arsenal exited the competition on penalties to the League Two sidee, Dowman was sent off for violent conduct for allegedly lashing out at Fleetwood defender Harrison Neal. The pair challenged for a couple of 50-50s before a brawl broke out.

Dowman then went down the tunnel and Arteta appeared to lean towards and say something to the teenager as he walked past. That treatment of the youngster was criticised by Paul Merson, who felt the Arsenal manager should have put an arm around him.
Asked what he said to Dowman, Arteta told reporters: "It was something that we discussed before the game." Arteta refused to go into any more detail on that when pressed on it.

On Sky Sports co-commentary duty, Andy Hinchcliffe said the red card was harsh on Dowman and Arteta replied: "I haven't seen it with the camera. You can't really see what happens. The decision was made by the referee and that's it.

articles.title: Glens secure Challenge Cup with Reds shootout win
articles.summary: Kelly Bailie scores the winning penalty for Glentoran in her final match to secure the Challenge Cup with a shootout win over Cliftonville at Windsor Park.
body: Bailie, 46, netted the final spot-kick in the shootout in her last game for the east Belfast club after 30 years.

The final had plenty of talking points in the build-up with Brendan Lynch's side being stripped of their League Cup title after they fielded two ineligible players against the Glens and the showpiece being delayed by three days due to Storm Boelo.
However, the final itself did not produce many memorable moments before the penalty shootout which the Glens won 4-2.
Cliftonville started the season finale on the front foot with Kirsty McGuinness' deflected shot, which had wrong-footed stopper Ellie Scott, going narrowly wide.

articles.title: Arsenal dumped out of Carabao Cup by League Two Fleetwood
articles.summary: Fleetwood Town produced one of the biggest shocks in Carabao Cup history as the League Two team dumped out Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties to reach the quarter-finals.
body: Mikel Arteta named a strong Arsenal side with Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front and Martin Odegaard playing the second half.
But they were not at the races, as the team two points above the League Two relegation zone took them to a 1-1 draw after Max Dowman was sent off before the shoot-out.
Then Bruno Guimaraes saw his penalty saved by Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch - who also made wonder saves to deny Ben White and Odegaard in stoppage time.
That left Conor Haughey to blast past Illan Meslier - picked by Arteta over penalty expert Kepa Arrizabalaga to make his Arsenal debut - to send Highbury mad.

articles.title: Spurs’ Julian Champagnie ties his own San Antonio record with bonkers first half vs. Kings
articles.summary: Kings appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Julian Champagnie has already made a habit of rewriting the San Antonio Spurs ’ record book from beyond the arc, and he did it again on Tuesday night against the Sacramento Kings.
body: Champagnie drilled eight 3-pointers in the first half at Frost Bank Center, tying his own franchise record for made threes in a half. The forward was nearly perfect, going 8-of-10 from deep and scoring all 24 of his first-half points from long range.
His barrage helped the Spurs pour in 80 points before the break and take an 80-54 lead into halftime.

Champagnie was hardly alone in the onslaught. Victor Wembanyama added 23 points on 11-of-18 shooting to go with nine rebounds and two blocks, while second-year guard Dylan Harper chipped in nine points and five rebounds. De’Aaron Fox added eight points and five assists.

As a team, San Antonio shot 60% from the field and knocked down 13 of its 22 attempts from three. The Spurs also piled up 23 assists against just four turnovers and outscored the Kings 41-25 in the second quarter, building a lead that reached 26 points.

articles.title: Yarde still targeting long-awaited showdown with Buatsi
articles.summary: Anthony Yarde is still targeting a fight with domestic rival Joshua Buatsi if he wins his clash with Willy Hutchinson for the vacant WBC light heavyweight world title.
body: Two years on from their first fight back in 2024, Buatsi takes on Hutchinson on November 7 at the AO Arena in Manchester.
Buatsi emerged victorious in their first meeting after dropping Hutchinson twice then winning via decision.
Now, Yarde is backing Buatsi to claim the win because that means they are one step closer to finally meeting in the ring.

Yarde has long been linked with a fight against his fellow light-heavyweight, with the two men seemingly on a collision course ever since Buatsi turned professional after winning bronze at the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.
